inventorySource.name: 2025 Federal Agency AI Use Case Inventory

portalNarrative.headline: A bounded FY 2026 program can materially accelerate FRUS.
portalNarrative.subhead: The most practical path is to adopt already-used federal AI patterns for clearance triage, research retrieval, metadata drafting, indexing, and editorial QA rather than attempt a wholesale platform rewrite.
portalNarrative.summary: This portal translates the federal AI inventory into a concrete FRUS delivery program built around achievable pilots and production assists that fit the existing TEI and HistoryAtState workflow.

frusFindings.headline: FRUS has four published production stages.
frusFindings.detail: History.state.gov describes the current FRUS flow as Planning, Research, Clearance, and Publication, with research explicitly covering archival research, selection, annotation, and review.

frusFindings.headline: Clearance is the biggest current bottleneck.
frusFindings.detail: The 2025 Report to Congress says declassification remains the single greatest obstacle to meeting the 30-year publication requirement; 46 volumes were in declassification review and 25 had been there for at least five years.

frusFindings.headline: FRUS is already moving toward incremental digital release.
frusFindings.detail: The 2025 report highlights a chapter-by-chapter publication approach so one uncleared chapter does not delay an entire volume, and the March 2025 HAC minutes note the first born-digital indexes across six volumes.

frusFindings.headline: HistoryAtState uses TEI, eXist-db, and XQuery as its digital publishing stack.
frusFindings.detail: The developer resources page states that article- and book-length content is encoded as TEI, stored in eXist-db, and converted into HTML and ebook forms with XQuery.

frusFindings.headline: The FRUS GitHub repo exposes canonical TEI sources and CI-generated publication artifacts.
frusFindings.detail: The FRUS repository explains that one TEI XML file represents a volume, document ids are canonical once released, tables of contents are generated automatically in CI, and releases are posted as soon as they are posted to history.state.gov.

frusFindings.headline: HistoryAtState runs a multi-repo build and deployment workflow.
frusFindings.detail: The hsg-project README describes history.state.gov as a multi-repository project built into eXist packages, while hsg-shell documents Node, Ant, Cypress, and automated release practices for the public website.

stageProfiles.title: Planning
stageProfiles.description: Grand conceptualization, volume conceptualization, backlog prioritization, release scheduling, and workload balancing.

stageProfiles.title: Research
stageProfiles.description: Collection, selection, annotation, and review of records across the national security establishment.

stageProfiles.title: Clearance
stageProfiles.description: Declassification coordination, redaction, sensitivity review, editing preparation, and release approvals.

stageProfiles.title: Publication
stageProfiles.description: Editing, indexing, metadata enhancement, chapter-based release, and public discovery on history.state.gov.

recommendedPortfolio.name: Semantic FRUS Research Workbench
recommendedPortfolio.why: FRUS researchers need faster discovery across distributed archival corpora and prior FRUS volumes.
recommendedPortfolio.frusBenefit: Reduce time spent locating candidate documents, support series planning, and improve chapter-level release sequencing.

recommendedPortfolio.name: Annotation and Metadata Copilot
recommendedPortfolio.why: Annotation, glossary work, provenance notes, and digital descriptions are labor-intensive and repetitive.
recommendedPortfolio.frusBenefit: Accelerate drafts for notes, term lists, person lists, and descriptive metadata while keeping historians in the loop.

recommendedPortfolio.name: Clearance and Redaction Triage Assistant
recommendedPortfolio.why: The Report to Congress identifies interagency declassification and redaction review as the main delay.
recommendedPortfolio.frusBenefit: Rank risky passages, surface likely equities, and cut reviewer time spent on low-risk material.

recommendedPortfolio.name: Incremental Publication and Discovery Tooling
recommendedPortfolio.why: FRUS is already publishing cleared chapters incrementally and experimenting with born-digital indexes.
recommendedPortfolio.frusBenefit: Improve chapter release packaging, index generation, and public discovery without waiting for whole-volume completion.

ideaFamilies.name: Semantic research and retrieval
ideaFamilies.summary: Natural-language search over prior FRUS volumes, archival descriptions, finding aids, and internal planning materials.
ideaFamilies.value: Cuts time spent locating candidate documents and helps historians start from relevant clusters instead of cold keyword search.

ideaFamilies.name: Metadata enrichment and descriptive drafting
ideaFamilies.summary: Generate draft descriptions, tags, and structured metadata for source packets, released chapters, and digital objects.
ideaFamilies.value: Reduces repetitive descriptive work and speeds handoff from research to publication.

ideaFamilies.name: Index, glossary, and entity extraction
ideaFamilies.summary: Extract people, organizations, terms, abbreviations, and topics for born-digital indexes and glossary drafts.
ideaFamilies.value: Supports chapter-by-chapter release and reduces the cost of compiling digital back matter.

ideaFamilies.name: Annotation and editorial drafting support
ideaFamilies.summary: Draft first-pass annotations, provenance notes, person notes, and editorial summaries from already-selected documents.
ideaFamilies.value: Keeps historians in the loop while shaving time off repetitive draft creation.

ideaFamilies.name: Clearance, redaction, and sensitivity triage
ideaFamilies.summary: Score passages for risk, suggest redaction candidates, and route reviewer attention to the most likely clearance blockers.
ideaFamilies.value: Directly addresses the biggest documented FRUS bottleneck: interagency declassification review.

ideaFamilies.name: Prior-release and FOIA precedent comparison
ideaFamilies.summary: Surface similar previously released text, related FOIA handling, and comparable redaction outcomes for reviewer reference.
ideaFamilies.value: Lets reviewers make faster, more consistent calls using their own release history.

ideaFamilies.name: Clustering, deduplication, and source-packet assembly
ideaFamilies.summary: Group related documents, identify near-duplicates and repeated passages, and assemble better candidate source packets.
ideaFamilies.value: Reduces manual sorting and helps editors focus on the most distinct, decision-relevant records.

ideaFamilies.name: OCR, transcription, and translation acceleration
ideaFamilies.summary: Accelerate intake for scanned or foreign-language material with draft text extraction, transcription, and translation.
ideaFamilies.value: Shortens the time from archival discovery to usable historian review copy.

ideaFamilies.name: TEI editorial QA and completeness checks
ideaFamilies.summary: Use AI-assisted checks to spot missing descriptions, incomplete reference structures, and publication-readiness gaps in TEI packages.
ideaFamilies.value: Improves chapter release quality without changing the core TEI and eXist stack.

ideaFamilies.name: Release-readiness routing and backlog management
ideaFamilies.summary: Track chapter readiness, blocked dependencies, and best-next release candidates using AI-assisted routing.
ideaFamilies.value: Supports FRUS's chapter-based publication approach and helps avoid all-or-nothing volume delays.

topProjectsFY26.name: FRUS Clearance Triage Assistant
topProjectsFY26.goal: Score passages for likely sensitivity, suggest candidate redactions, and route reviewer attention toward the most likely blockers.
topProjectsFY26.whyAchievable: This can be piloted on already digitized chapter sets and existing reviewer queues without changing final release authority.
topProjectsFY26.frusImpact: Reduces low-risk manual review load and helps cut time spent on volumes stuck in declassification review.
deliverables: Audit log for accepted and rejected suggestions

topProjectsFY26.name: Semantic FRUS Research Workbench
topProjectsFY26.goal: Provide semantic retrieval across prior FRUS volumes, finding aids, editorial memos, and archival descriptions.
topProjectsFY26.whyAchievable: It can start with a bounded corpus and read-only retrieval layer, which avoids risky workflow replacement.
topProjectsFY26.frusImpact: Helps historians find relevant records and comparable prior work faster, reducing search overhead during compilation planning and document selection.
deliverables: Vector or semantic index for a bounded FRUS corpus
Source citation links back to volumes and finding aids

topProjectsFY26.name: Metadata Autofill for Source Packets
topProjectsFY26.goal: Generate draft descriptions, tags, and structured metadata for research packets and released chapters.
topProjectsFY26.whyAchievable: The work is bounded, historian-reviewable, and already mirrors what NARA is piloting for archival descriptions.
topProjectsFY26.frusImpact: Speeds research handoffs, improves discoverability, and reduces repetitive catalog-style drafting.

topProjectsFY26.name: Born-Digital Index and Glossary Builder
topProjectsFY26.goal: Extract people, organizations, terms, abbreviations, and topics to produce draft born-digital indexes and glossary entries.
topProjectsFY26.whyAchievable: FRUS is already experimenting with born-digital indexes, so this extends an existing direction instead of inventing a new one.
topProjectsFY26.frusImpact: Supports faster chapter release and reduces the long-tail labor of creating digital back matter.
deliverables: Draft index entries with source references

topProjectsFY26.name: Annotation Draft Copilot
topProjectsFY26.goal: Draft first-pass annotations, provenance notes, and explanatory summaries from already-selected documents and reference material.
topProjectsFY26.whyAchievable: The scope can be restricted to draft generation with mandatory historian review before any text is accepted.
topProjectsFY26.frusImpact: Reduces repeated drafting effort and shortens the distance from document selection to publishable editorial copy.

topProjectsFY26.name: Prior-Release and FOIA Precedent Comparator
topProjectsFY26.goal: Find similar previously released passages and comparable FOIA-style handling so reviewers can assess consistency faster.
topProjectsFY26.whyAchievable: The first version can rely on retrieval and similarity scoring over previously released material, with no automatic clearance decisions.
topProjectsFY26.frusImpact: Improves consistency and reduces the need to rediscover how similar text was previously handled.
deliverables: Similarity search over released FRUS text

topProjectsFY26.name: Duplicate Detection and Document Clustering
topProjectsFY26.goal: Cluster related documents, flag near duplicates, and surface the most distinct items for inclusion decisions.
topProjectsFY26.whyAchievable: This can run as an offline analyst-assist process over selected batches without changing historian workflows.
topProjectsFY26.frusImpact: Reduces manual sorting and helps editors spend more time on high-value documentary choices.

topProjectsFY26.name: OCR, Transcription, and Translation Intake Lane
topProjectsFY26.goal: Create a historian-reviewable intake lane for scanned or foreign-language material that produces draft text and translation.
topProjectsFY26.whyAchievable: A bounded pilot can target selected document sets where manual text creation is currently delaying historian review.
topProjectsFY26.frusImpact: Shortens the time between archival discovery and usable editorial review copy.

topProjectsFY26.name: TEI Editorial QA Assistant
topProjectsFY26.goal: Check TEI packages for missing descriptions, broken reference patterns, incomplete metadata, and publication-readiness issues.
topProjectsFY26.whyAchievable: It builds on the existing TEI workflow and can begin as an advisory preflight check instead of a publishing-system rewrite.
topProjectsFY26.frusImpact: Improves consistency and reduces avoidable cleanup work late in the release cycle.

topProjectsFY26.name: Chapter Release Readiness Cockpit
topProjectsFY26.goal: Show which chapters are publishable now, what is blocked, and what sequence yields the fastest public release gains.
topProjectsFY26.whyAchievable: FRUS already has a chapter-based release strategy, so this is a routing and visibility layer over an existing policy direction.
topProjectsFY26.frusImpact: Helps prevent one blocked chapter from stalling the public release value of otherwise ready work.
